SMTO-EXE-0205 — The PDF action failed for an unclear reason

GUID: b2f0cedd-8e27-5d23-8b93-d4ee2ea80fb1
Slug: pdf-operation-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • Something went wrong while working on the PDF, and SMTO couldn't tell exactly what. Your original PDF was not changed and no new file was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO for basic information about the PDF, such as how many pages it has. If that works, the file is readable and the problem is with the specific action you asked for.
  2. Try the same action on a different, simple PDF. If that works, something particular to your original file is triggering the failure.
  3. Select Copy error details and note the exact message you sent SMTO. This message does not establish the cause, so the person fixing it needs to repeat the same action on the same kind of file.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the PDF action and shows its result or a new file under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details, your message to SMTO and, if you're allowed to share it, the PDF to the person who manages SMTO. Keep the original file unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway PDF worker raised an unrecognized exception that maps to operation_failed; no narrower cause (bad input, limits, permissions) was identified and no output was published.

What this means

  • PDF exception translation found no narrower recognized local failure and returned operation_failed. The category alone does not identify a bad input document or resource shortage. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF exception translation found no narrower recognized local failure and returned operation_failed. The category alone does not identify a bad input document or resource shortage.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation, bounded diagnostics and original output state before attributing it to input size or document structure.

How to fix it

  • Treat this as a probable defect: gateway_core/pdf/common.failure() returns operation_failed only for exceptions it does not classify, and parser exception text is deliberately suppressed. Reproduce with the same PDF, operation and arguments on the same Gateway (try pdf.info first), preserve the source file, and report the reproduction with the error details.
  • Preserve sources and inspect the original failure and outputs; report a reproducible backend defect when no supported remedy is established.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the bounded PDF receipt and input, reduce the request if needed, and retry only after resolving the reported condition.

How to verify the fix

  • The specific failed prerequisite is established and supported work completes with a valid receipt.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
